dedupe_keys.name: epa public water system service area boundaries

description: This dataset maps the geographic areas served by US public water systems. EPA's Office of Research and Development built it, and the Office of Water now maintains it, so that system data reported under the Safe Drinking Water Act (violations, population served) can be linked to the people and places each system serves. It covers over 44,000 community water systems in all 50 states, Washington DC, territories and tribal lands, about 99 per cent of the population they serve; version 3 (17 March 2026) added about 78,000 transient and non-transient non-community systems, mapped at parcel level, around 84 per cent of that universe. About 60 per cent of community boundaries come from state or utility sources and about 40 per cent were modelled by EPA with machine learning from building footprints, population density and connections. Each polygon carries the PWSID, population, connections and boundary source. Access: free zipped download and R code on GitHub (MIT), ArcGIS feature services and a web map. Caveats: modelled boundaries are estimates that often differ from real ones, EPA does not warrant spatial accuracy, many tribal and territorial systems are missing, private wells are not shown, and the repository labels the work as pre-dissemination peer review. Simulation uses: linking drinking-water assets and outages to served populations, exposure of service areas to hazards, emergency response and investment planning. Related records: HIFLD Open (data-hifld-open) for other US infrastructure layers.
